narrative.overview:
periscope is a quiet grey field that agents show up on. Most of the time nothing on it is lit: surfaces, rules and text all sit in one cool, nearly colourless grey (hue 250, chroma under 0.010). When an agent has something to report, it appears as a coloured blip: an orange ping when it needs you, a green contact when it is done, an amber sweep while it works. The field exists so those blips can't be missed, and a screen that adds colour for any other reason has broken the instrument.

The density is that of a tool you live in all day. Body text is 13px, metadata 10–11px, rows have 3–9px of vertical padding, and the whole dashboard is one split view: the rail on the left, the live pane on the right, a header strip above. Controls are compact and tactile: small pills, keycaps with a thicker bottom edge, segmented pins. They stay muted until hovered or chosen. The interface is dark only; there is no light theme.

The one place the instrument lets personality in is Clawd's device in the header's top-right corner. It is a pixel-art critter inside its own bezel that keeps a daily schedule, holds up the most urgent item and takes you there when clicked. It is part of the identity, not a decoration. Its frame keeps it visibly separate from the work around it.

**Rejected looks** (confirmed): SaaS analytics dashboards (KPI tiles, decorative charts, gradient hero cards, airy spacing); neon hacker terminals (green on black, glow, scanlines); colour used as decoration.
keyCharacteristics: A cool grey field, made of one hue at very low chroma, with depth built from tonal steps.
Colour means a state or a kind of thing, never ornament.
Every status colour has the same lightness, so urgency comes from motion and position rather than brightness.
One interactive accent (Periscope Glass) for selection, focus and "active".
Sans for labels and prose, mono for anything you could paste: refs, paths and commands.
Compact, tactile controls: pills, keycaps, segmented pins.
Unicode glyphs instead of an icon set (◆ ◇ $ ✻ ⬡ ⎇ ★), each coloured by the kind of thing it marks.
Clawd lives in a bezel: personality is welcome but framed.

rules.name: The Blip Rule
rules.body: Colour on the field is a signal: either a state, or a kind of thing (repo, track, branch, ticket, account). A hue that reports nothing doesn't ship.

rules.name: The Same-Brightness Rule
rules.body: Status hues sit at lightness 0.74–0.80 and chroma 0.13–0.17, and differ only in hue. No state wins by being brighter. Urgency comes from the pulse and from position (NEEDS YOU sits at the top of the rail).

rules.name: The One Glass Rule
rules.body: Periscope Glass is the only interactive accent. Selection, focus, active and drop targets use it. Agent state never does.

rules.name: The Mixed-Tint Rule
rules.body: Build a tint by mixing a token into transparent (`color-mix(in oklch, <token> 16%, transparent)`), the way the `-bg` tokens are built. Transparent has no hue, so the token keeps its own. When the tint must be opaque, mix into the surface `in srgb` (as the drop-target wash does). Mixing into a grey surface `in oklch` swings the hue toward the grey's 250: the danger button's red mix comes out violet. The attention rows' tinted backgrounds (`#241316`, `#122019`, `#1d1a10`, `#161a14`) are still hard-coded hex near those mixes. Both are drift, not patterns to copy.

rules.name: The Paste-It Rule
rules.body: If the user could copy a value into a terminal (a PR number, ticket ID, branch, path or command), set it in `--mono`. Labels, status and prose stay `--sans`.

rules.name: The Organizer Rule
rules.body: UPPERCASE letter-spaced 10px text only labels a section; it is never content. A track name shown as a label is uppercase; the same name inside a sentence is not.

rules.name: The Column Rule
rules.body: A pane's metadata lines (cwd chip, narrator status, PR and ticket chips) each take a full line, indented 21px so they start under the label (14px icon plus a 7px gap). Fields stay in one column from row to row, and never share a line in a way that makes their position depend on content length.

rules.name: The Tonal Stack Rule
rules.body: Surfaces separate by lightness step, not by shadow. If a new container needs to read as raised, move it one `bg-` step up.

rules.name: The Only-What-Floats Rule
rules.body: Ambient shadows belong to menus, toasts, modals and the one lifted pane. Nothing that sits in the layout gets a drop shadow.

dos: **Do** keep every surface in the cool-grey family (hue 250, chroma ≤ 0.010) and build depth by stepping through `bg-0` → `bg-1` → `bg-2`.

**Do** give each hue a single meaning everywhere it appears: Periscope Glass for interaction, Track Magenta for tracks, Worktree Violet for branches, Ticket Purple for tickets, Account Teal for accounts, and the sonar colours for state.
**Do** put any new status colour on the shared brightness (lightness 0.74–0.80, chroma 0.13–0.17) and vary only its hue.
**Do** derive tints with `color-mix(in oklch, <token> N%, transparent)`, or `in srgb` when mixing into an opaque surface, instead of adding new hex values.
**Do** set refs, paths, branches and commands in `--mono`, and check every new size in every face on the Settings → Fonts list.
**Do** show shortcuts as keycaps (the 2px bottom edge).
**Do** register every new animation in the `prefers-reduced-motion` block.
**Do** keep critters inside a bezel or their own frame wherever they appear.
**Do** match `bg-term` (`#282c34`) exactly on anything that frames a terminal canvas.
donts: **Don't** use colour as decoration. If a hue isn't reporting a state or marking a kind of thing, it doesn't ship.
**Don't** reach for SaaS analytics vocabulary: KPI tiles, decorative charts, gradient hero cards, generous empty spacing around a few numbers.
**Don't** go neon hacker terminal: no green on black, glow, scanlines or "cyber" styling.
**Don't** add a second interactive accent, and don't use Periscope Glass to report agent state.
**Don't** make one state louder than another by brightness. Urgency comes from the pulse and from position.
**Don't** pulse or loop anything in the work surface except needs-input and done.
**Don't** put drop shadows on things that sit in the layout. Shadows are for menus, toasts, modals and the one lifted pane.
**Don't** add half-pixel type sizes or new hard-coded hex values. Both exist today as drift, not as patterns.
